paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between iteration number and loss for several different configurations. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels every 20000 units. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels every 0.1 units. A purple line represents “Vanilla,” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.65 at an iteration of 140000, exhibiting a steep decline in the first 20000 iterations followed by a more gradual decrease. A blue line represents “StrmLLM (n=64),” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.66 at an iteration of 140000, with a similar pattern to the purple line. An orange line represents “SepLLM (n=64),” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.67 at an iteration of 140000, also displaying a steep initial decline and a subsequent gradual decrease. A green line represents “SepLLM (n=64, H),” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.66 at an iteration of 140000, and remaining relatively stable between iterations 60000 and 140000. A pink line represents “SepLLM (n=64, H/T),” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and remaining roughly constant after 40000 iterations, fluctuating between approximately 2.64 and 2.67 at an iteration of 140000. A dark blue line represents “SepLLM (n=128),” starting at approximately 3.33 at an iteration of 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.68 at an iteration of 140000, showing a similar initial decline as the other lines followed by a stabilization.
